Fit one specification end to end

Source: R/fit_spec.R
fit_spec.Rd

Specification in, run out: builds the estimator inputs with build_setup(), fits, runs inference, and – given a store – saves the whole run so it can be reloaded and re-plotted without refitting.

Usage

fit_spec(
  spec,
  panel,
  store = NULL,
  keep = c("all", "est", "none"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

spec

An sdid_spec().

panel

An sdid_panel().

store

Directory of a run store to save into, or NULL.

keep

How much of the fit to retain: "all" (default) keeps the fitted object and every placebo draw, which every plot needs; "est" keeps only the fitted object; "none" keeps the summary alone.

seed

NULL to inherit the caller's RNG stream, or an integer seed applied to this fit only.

Value

An sdid_run: spec, spec_hash, run_id, fit, pool, balance, periods, timings and meta.

Reproducibility of the standard error

Placebo standard errors are simulated, so they depend on the state of the RNG stream when the fit begins. seed = NULL inherits the caller's stream: reproducible for a whole sweep run after one set.seed(), but a spec refitted on its own gets a different SE. Passing seed = seed_for(spec) makes a spec reproducible in isolation. The caller's own stream is left untouched either way.

Examples

# \donttest{
spec <- sdid_spec(label = "Prop 99", inference = list(replications = 50))
run <- fit_spec(spec, prop99_panel(), seed = 1)
run
#> 
#> ── sdid_run Prop 99 
#> • ATT -15.6 95% CI [-37.4, 6.18]
#> • SE 11.1 (t = -1.40)
#> • fit sdid, N0 = 38, T0 = 19, pre-period RMSE 1.73
#> • placebos 47/50 kept at trim_k 5
#> • treated California from 1989
#> • spec bf7b1f5e74c4 run 20260929T053936906476-bf7b1f5e
# }
